1  CRL.P No. 1952 of 2024

THIS CRL.P IS FILED U/S.482 OF CR.P.C PRAYING TO QUASH THE PROCEEDINGS INITIATED AGAINST THE PETITIONER IN THEIR CR.NO.24/2019 IN SPL.C.C.NO.146/2019 ON THE FILE OF LXX ADDITIONAL CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE AND SPECIAL JUDGE,
BENGALURU (CCH-71) BY THE 1ST RESPONDENT YESHWANTHPURA POLICE STATION, BENGALURU FOR THE ALLEGED OFFENCE P/U/S 376, 417 AND 420 OF IPC AND SEC.
3(1)(r)(s) AND (w) AND SEC. 3(ii)(v) OF SC/ST (POA) ACT.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

Petitioner is before this Court with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings in Spl.C.C.
No.146/2019 pending before the Court of LXX Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge and Special Judge at Bangalore (CCH-71) arising out of Crime No.24/2019 registered by Yeshawanthpura police station, Bengaluru, for offences punishable under Sections 376, 417, 420 of IPC and Section 3(1)
(r)(s) and (w), 3(ii)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 2015.

entities.text: Court of LXX Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge and Special Judge at Bangalore (CCH-71)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3. FIR in Crime No.24/2019 was registered by Yeshawanthpura Police Station, Bengaluru City for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 417, 420 of IPC and Section 3(1) (r)(s) and (w), 3(ii)(v)
of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) NC: 2024:KHC:10620 Act, 2015 against the petitioner herein on the complaint of respondent No.2 herein, who was aged about 22 years as on the date of the complaint.
In the complaint, it is averred that complainant belongs to Schedule Caste and the petitioner is a Vokkaliga.
Petitioner and the complainant were acquainted to each other and they were in love.
The petitioner allegedly assured the complainant that he will marry her and took her with him to hotels, cinema, park etc.

On 07.01.2019, at about 10 p.m, the petitioner allegedly took the complainant in his two wheeler and at about 10.45 p.m., they checked-in into Room No.212 of Hotel Grand Arebian near Yeshwanthpura Market.

In the said room, complainant allegedly drank a juice which was provided to her by the petitioner and after drinking the same, she lost her conscious and when she gained conscious, she realized that the petitioner had sexually assaulted her.
When the complainant questioned the petitioner, he assured that he would marry her.

Thereafter, on 12.01.2019 when the complainant asked the petitioner to marry her, petitioner allegedly refused stating that she belongs to Schedule Caste and his mother had proposed some other girl and he would be marrying her.

It is in this background, the complainant had NC: 2024:KHC:10620 approached the police on 15.01.2019 and lodged a complaint which had resulted in registering FIR in Crime No.24/2019 by Yeshwanthapura Police Station, for the aforesaid offences.

2 4.

Learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the respondent No.2 jointly submit that dispute between the petitioner and respondent No.2 has been settled amicably out of Court and both of them have now decided to live separately.
They intend to give a quietus to the dispute and also end their relationship.
They submit that parties have filed a joint memo under Section 320 r/w 482 of Cr.P.C. with a prayer to quash the entire impugned proceedings.
The joint memo filed by the petitioner and the respondent No.2 which is signed by their respective advocates and supported by the joint affidavit of the parties is taken on record.
The petitioner and the respondent No.2 who are present in person before the Court are identified by their respective advocates.

In paragraphs 3 to 6 of the joint memo which is supported by the joint affidavit of the parties it is stated as follows:
" 3.
It is further submits that, both the parties i.e., petitioner and the respondent No.2 have NC: 2024:KHC:10620 agreed to settle the disputes pending between each other amicably out of the court.
Both the petitioner No.1 and the second respondent have mutually agreed to live separately by withdrawing the allegations made against each other.
Both of them have agreed that they will not interfere with each other in their personal life and both of them have no objection to lead an independent life as per their choice.

4. It is further submits that, in terms of the settlement arrived between the parties,
the respondent No.2 has agreed to withdraw the proceedings pending in Crime No.24/2019 in SPL.C.C. No.146/2019 of 1st respondent police on the file of LXX Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge and Special Judge at Bangalore (CCH-71), against the petitioner.

As such the respondent No.2 has no objection to allow the present petition and quash the proceedings in Crime No.24/2019 in SPL.C.C. No.146/2019 of 1st respondent police on the file of LXX Addl. City Civil and sessions Judge and special Judge at Bangalore (CCH-71), of 1st respondent police.

entities.text: LXX Addl. City Civil and sessions Judge and special Judge at Bangalore (CCH-71)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 5. It is further submitted that, similarly, both the parties have no future claims against each other.
It is further submits that, the parties have affixed their signatures with their free consent without having any misrepresentation, fraud and undue influence."

5. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ramgopal and another vs. State Of Madhya Pradesh reported in AIR 2022 (14) SCC 531 has held that even in respect of non- compoundable offences if the allegations made in the criminal case are private in nature, to secure complete justice, the High Court in exercise of its inherent power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. can quash the proceedings having regard to the settlement arrived between the parties, which is voluntary, without there being any undue influence and coercion.

entities.text: Ramgopal and another vs. State Of Madhya Pradesh reported in AIR 2022 (14) SCC 531
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ramgopal (Supra) has observed as under:
Karthik vs State Of Karnataka By on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169512381/
3 "11.

sentences.text: True it is that offences which are "non- compoundable" cannot be compounded by a criminal court in purported exercise of its powers under Section 320CrPC.
Any such attempt by the court would amount to alteration, addition and modification of Section 320CrPC, which is the exclusive domain of legislature.

There is no patent or latent ambiguity in the language of Section 320CrPC, which may justify its wider NC:
2024:KHC:10620 interpretation and include such offences in the docket of "compoundable" offences which have been consciously kept out as non-compoundable.

Nevertheless, the limited jurisdiction to compound an offence within the framework of Section 320CrPC is not an embargo against invoking inherent powers by the High Court vested in it under Section 482CrPC.

The High Court, keeping in view the peculiar facts and circumstances of a case and for justifiable reasons can press Section 482CrPC in aid to prevent abuse of the process of any court and/or to secure the ends of justice.

12. The High Court, therefore, having regard to the nature of the offence and the fact that parties have amicably settled their dispute and the victim has willingly consented to the nullification of criminal proceedings, can quash such proceedings in exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482CrPC, even if the offences are non-compoundable.

The High Court can indubitably evaluate the consequential effects of the offence beyond the body of an individual and thereafter adopt a pragmatic approach, to ensure that the felony, even if goes unpunished, does not tinker with or paralyse the very object of the administration of criminal justice system.
xxxxxxxxxx 19.

We thus sum up and hold that as opposed to Section 320CrPC where the Court is squarely guided by the compromise between the parties in respect of NC:
2024:KHC:10620 offences "compoundable" within the statutory framework, the extraordinary power enjoined upon a High Court under Section 482CrPC or vested in this Court under Article 142 of the Constitution, can be invoked beyond the metes and bounds of Section 320CrPC.

By on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169512381/
4 7.

The respondent No.2 complainant, who is present before the Court on enquiry has stated that out of her own volition, without there being any coercion and undue influence she has signed the joint memo and produced the same before this Court.

Considering the nature of allegations in the complaint and having regard to the fact that the allegations made against the petitioner are private in nature and the dispute between the NC: 2024:KHC:10620 parties is now settled at the intervention of elders and well wishers of both the parties and the parties have decided to give a quietus to the dispute and live separately without interfering with each others' life, I am of the opinion that the prayer made in the joint memo as well as in the petition is required to be allowed.
Accordingly the following ORDER The criminal petition is allowed.

The entire proceedings in Spl.C.C. No.146/2019 pending before the Court of LXX Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge and Special Judge at Bangalore (CCH-71) arising out of Crime No.24/2019 registered by Yeshawanthpura police station, Bengaluru, for offences punishable under Sections 376, 417, 420 of IPC and Section 3(1) (r)(s) and (w), 3(ii)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 2015 is quashed.
